QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_37

question.text: An AIF reports PIC = 0.90 in its quarterly LP letter. What does this indicate?

answer.text: The fund is about to complete its final close
The fund has drawn down most of its capital commitments from LPs
The fund has 90% recovery rate on its investments
The fund has only 10% NPA exposure

explanation.text: **The Logic:** PIC = Paid-in / Committed = 0.90 means 90% of committed capital has been CALLED DOWN. Signals the fund is near the end of its drawdown/investment phase. **The Trap:** Option A confuses drawdown with raising. Option D is a credit metric, not PIC. Option C conflates PIC with DPI. **Cross-Exam Context:** This exact question appears in XIX-C sample; XIX-A/B tests similar. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** At PIC ~0.90, start communicating your vintage-year IRR to LPs — their allocation committees use this checkpoint to decide on commit-to-next-fund timing.
